site.name: tablerose
site.summary: tablerose-clone Fictional restaurant reservation platform "Tablerose" multi-page booking flow. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Discovery: hero with 5-field search card (city autocomplete / party / date / time); 5 quick-pill suggestions; 6-card "reserved most this week" trending grid; 4-card editor guides; 3-step "how it works" | | `restaurants.html` | Results: top reservation summary bar with Edit; left filter rail (8 cuisines, 4 price tiers, 6 neighborhoods, 6 features); 10-row results list with photo / name / stars / blurb / tags / per-row time slots (slots within ±30min of search are highlighted, others muted); sort dropdown (relevance / rating / price / distance) | | `restaurant.html` | Detail: split hero (photo / info with stars / dress / hours); 4 tabs (Overview with about, highlights table; Menu with 3 sections; Photos with 9 swatches; Reviews with rating bars + 3 reviews); right-side sticky booking card (date / party / 10 time slots — 30min near target highlighted, 17:00/21:30 disabled for Bella Suora); SVG mini-map; favorite heart toggle |

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore Tablerose’s reservation journey from discovery through confirmation, while also validating adjacent discovery/results/detail interactions and key recovery/edit states on both desktop and mobile.
run_plan.summary: Start from the homepage and confirm the primary discovery-to-booking funnel works: search or browse into results, open a restaurant, choose a time, provide guest details, complete the card-hold step, and land on confirmation. Along the way, probe adjacent entry points such as quick suggestion pills, trending cards, editorial guides, filters, sorting, restaurant tabs, favorites, and confirmation actions. Reserve extra attention for time-slot availability rules, summary persistence between steps, and the many small tap targets already hinted at in prescan for mobile usability.
assumptions: The core primary flow is index.html → restaurants.html → restaurant.html → guest.html → payment.html → confirmation.html.
Links with href '#' in the header likely do not navigate to additional HTML pages and should be treated as low-priority/non-core unless they reveal inline behavior.

The same restaurant data appears reused across discovery, results, detail, and checkout steps, so consistency of restaurant name, date, time, party size, fees, and cancellation cutoff should be validated across pages.
Because the site is a static multi-page clone, some controls may simulate state rather than perform full backend validation; the run should still inspect visible UX feedback and state continuity.
risk_hotspots: index.html search card: WHERE/PARTY/DATE/TIME inputs plus Find tables button as the main entry to booking
index.html quick suggestion pills and trending/editorial cards that all route into restaurants.html and may create repetitive or unclear entry states
restaurants.html filter rail with 8 cuisines, 4 price tiers, 6 neighborhoods, and 6 features; high risk for state stacking, reset behavior, and scanability
restaurants.html sort control (relevance/rating/price/distance) and whether list ordering/labels change understandably
restaurants.html per-row time-slot buttons, especially highlighted near-target slots versus muted alternatives
restaurant.html sticky booking card with date/party/time slots, including disabled times (17:00 and 21:30 for Bella Suora) and selection clarity
restaurant.html tabs (Overview/Menu/Photos/Reviews) for content switching, state persistence, and discoverability
restaurant.html favorite heart/save toggle for reversible state and visibility
guest.html long form with many inputs, dietary checkboxes, occasion choices, marketing/reminder opt-in, and special request character count
payment.html payment-method switcher (Card/Apple Pay/Google Pay), card fields, add-ons, and no-show fee explanation
confirmation.html visible data integrity issue risk: prescan shows text 'at for undefined guest', so booking summary rendering needs explicit validation
confirmation.html post-booking actions: add to calendar options, resend email, modify, cancel

phases.title: Discovery and entry-point mapping
phases.objective: Validate the homepage as a clear starting point for finding a table and identify which entry points feed the booking flow most effectively.
key_checks: Exercise the main search card: inspect WHERE, PARTY, DATE, TIME controls and submit via Find tables
Open at least one quick suggestion pill and confirm it lands in results with a coherent reservation context
Open at least one trending restaurant card and confirm it deep-links into restaurant detail
Open at least one editor guide card and confirm it routes into results rather than a dead end
Inspect top-nav items that point to real pages versus '#' placeholders; avoid spending run budget on clearly inert header links
Note first-impression clarity around the promise of card hold/no-show policy before booking begins
exit_criteria: At least three distinct homepage entry types have been exercised: search, suggestion/editorial link, and restaurant card
Observed whether discovery entry points preserve or ignore chosen search context

phases.title: Results refinement and restaurant selection
phases.objective: Validate that results are understandable, refinable, and actionable enough to choose a reservation without confusion.
key_checks: Verify top summary bar shows city, party size, date, and time, and inspect the Edit affordance if it exposes a way to revise search context
Apply a small mix of filters across different groups (for example cuisine + price + feature) and confirm visible results/count updates sensibly
Use Reset filters and confirm the list returns to baseline
Change sort order at least twice and check whether ordering/labels respond clearly
Inspect highlighted versus muted per-row time slots for availability cues and click one slot to enter restaurant detail or continue selection
Open at least two different restaurant rows to compare consistency of information scent from results to detail
exit_criteria: Multiple filter groups and reset behavior have been exercised
Sort has been changed and observed
At least one selection path from results into restaurant detail has been validated

phases.title: Restaurant detail and time selection
phases.objective: Validate that a diner can evaluate a restaurant and confidently choose a reservation time from the detail page.
key_checks: Review the hero information for clarity and consistency with results data: cuisine, price, area, rating, hours, address, and booking popularity
Switch through all four tabs (Overview, Menu, Photos, Reviews) and confirm content changes appropriately without losing context
Test the save/favorite heart toggle for visible state change and reversibility
Use the booking card controls for date and party size if available, then select several time-slot states: available, highlighted-near-target, and disabled
Explicitly verify Bella Suora’s disabled slots (17:00 and 21:30) are visually distinct and non-actionable
Check whether the sticky booking card remains usable while scrolling through long content
Proceed from a chosen slot into guest.html and verify the selected restaurant/date/time/party carry forward
exit_criteria: All detail tabs have been visited
Save toggle and booking controls have been exercised
A valid time selection has successfully advanced into guest.html

phases.title: Guest details and hold step
phases.objective: Validate form completion UX, reservation-summary continuity, and transparency of payment/hold policies before finalizing the booking.
key_checks: On guest.html, complete key personal fields and interact with optional controls: at least one dietary option, one occasion option, and special request text entry
Observe the special request character counter behavior while typing
Check the reservation summary card on guest.html for correctness and readability, including cancel-by timing and card-hold messaging
Use the back link once if practical to verify users can recover without losing critical selections, then continue forward again
On payment.html, switch between Card, Apple Pay, and Google Pay options if those controls change the UI
Fill visible card fields and inspect whether add-ons update the reservation summary or total clearly
Verify the no-show fee explanation, authorization amount, and cancellation deadline are understandable and consistent with previous steps
Submit Hold the table to reach confirmation.html
exit_criteria: Guest form has been meaningfully completed and advanced
Payment method options and at least one add-on have been exercised

phases.title: Confirmation and recovery actions
phases.objective: Validate booking completion, post-booking reassurance, and recovery options such as modify/cancel/resend.
key_checks: Confirm booking success messaging and verify all summary fields render correctly; explicitly inspect the prescan-suspect text around restaurant/time/guest count
Try calendar actions (Apple, Google, Outlook) and note whether they behave as visible affordances or dead-end controls
Use Resend email and check for immediate confirmation feedback
Exercise Modify and Cancel actions to assess whether recovery paths are presented clearly
Inspect before-you-go guidance and special-request/dietary recap for consistency with entered data
Use recommendation links or Back to discover only after core confirmation actions have been validated
exit_criteria: Confirmation summary integrity has been checked
At least two post-booking actions have been exercised
One recovery/control path from confirmation has been inspected

phases.title: Mobile-critical pass
phases.objective: Repeat the most important booking interactions on mobile to uncover responsiveness, tap-target, and sticky-layout issues.
key_checks: Revisit index.html on mobile and retest search card entry plus at least one suggestion pill, paying attention to stacked layout and already-flagged small tap targets in the header and quick pills
On restaurants.html mobile, verify filter rail/access, sort usability, density of result rows, and time-slot tapability
On restaurant.html mobile, verify tab navigation, sticky booking card behavior, save toggle access, and disabled slot clarity
On guest.html and payment.html mobile, inspect form field spacing, checkbox/radio tap sizes, keyboard flow, and whether the reservation summary crowds primary actions
On confirmation.html mobile, validate readability of post-booking actions and any truncation/overlap in summary content
exit_criteria: Critical booking path has been spot-checked on mobile from discovery through confirmation
Known small-tap-target areas from prescan have been visually confirmed or disproven in mobile layout
At least one mobile-specific usability issue or reassurance point has been documented for each major funnel stage

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 6 known HTML pages, with repeated visits to restaurants.html and restaurant.html via different entry points.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls on core pages: homepage search and browse links; results filters, reset, sort, and time slots; restaurant tabs, save toggle, booking card; guest form options; payment methods and add-ons; confirmation actions.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the critical discovery-to-booking flow on mobile with emphasis on small tap targets, dense result rows, sticky booking controls, and long-form completion.

notes: Favor depth on the booking funnel over exhaustive clicking of repeated restaurant cards that likely share the same destination.
Because prescan shows no console or network issues, prioritize UX/state integrity and content consistency rather than technical failure hunting.
Explicitly capture any mismatch in date/time formats, guest count, cancellation policy, authorization amount, or restaurant identity as the user moves between pages.
If Modify/Cancel from confirmation re-enters earlier steps, treat that as a recovery path rather than a separate new flow.

ux_notes: Clicking the quick pill successfully navigates to restaurants.html, but the results context stays generic: the summary bar still reads 'Portland, OR · 2 guests · Sat, May 16 · 7:00 pm' and the page shows '10 restaurants' with no visible 'Pasta' query, preselected cuisine filter, or explanation of why these results match the shortcut.

The destination creates coherence issues for reservation context because several visible reservation chips are early-morning times like '6:00 am', '6:30 am', and '7:00 am' even though the carried search context says '7:00 pm', which can make the shortcut feel unreliable.

This action also surfaces precision/accessibility risk on the results page: the 'Edit' control is only 25x16px and cuisine checkboxes are 13x13px per layout warnings, making key recovery/filter actions harder to tap, especially on mobile.

step.objective: Learn whether selecting a cuisine filter gives immediate, understandable feedback in the results list and helps reconcile the generic Pasta shortcut destination.

ux_notes: Submitting the homepage search successfully lands on Restaurants and preserves the search summary at the top as "Portland, OR · 1 guest · Sat, May 16 · 7:00 pm," so the carried-over context is visible on the results page.

The results context is internally inconsistent with the selected time: despite the header showing 7:00 pm, listing availability chips are rendered as morning times like "6:00 am," "6:30 am," "7:00 am," and "8:15 am," which creates a strong mismatch between what users think they searched for and what results imply.
The page exposes an "Edit" control for changing the carried-over search, but its hit area is very small (25x16px per layout warning), making correction harder if users notice the time mismatch.

step.objective: Learn whether the Sushi quick-suggestion on mobile lands in results that clearly reflect sushi intent and exposes mobile tap-target or context issues.
step.success_criteria: restaurants.html loads in mobile view with visible results context, allowing assessment of intent match, summary clarity, and mobile control density.
